stem:
Wasim draws the equilateral triangle shown in the figure. He wants to count its lines of symmetry by testing folds.

How many lines of symmetry does the equilateral triangle have?

options.text: Three: each line from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side passes the fold test.
Infinitely many, because any line through the centre looks balanced at a glance.
Three folds are what create the equilateral triangle in the first place.
The count needs group-theory language before any fold can be checked.

teacher.key_rationale: An equilateral triangle has exactly three fold lines, each from a vertex to the opposite midpoint. Counting infinitely many omits the fold test. Saying folds create the triangle reverses the relation. Requiring group-theory language over-extends the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as an equilateral triangle with three dashed candidate fold lines.
